allowed_errors.meaning: The Opentrons analyzer returned result not-ok and included structured error records.
The protocol attempted an impossible deck or fixture placement, such as loading a module into an occupied or incompatible deck area.
The protocol used an operation gated behind an API level newer than the installed Opentrons package supports.
The agent attempted to start or control live Opentrons hardware instead of staying within captured protocol-analysis dry-run evidence.
A reproduced analyzer fixture no longer matches the captured command family, package version, or protocol artifact.

dry_run_semantics: Fixtures are captured local analyzer responses from opentrons==9.1.0 using python -m opentrons.cli analyze against the protocol files in this pack.
Captured outputs are protocol-analysis dry runs: they expose command plans, labware, pipettes, modules, liquids, errors, and placement constraints without moving hardware.

Positive fixtures cover liquid handling, waste chute use, module temperature control, heater-shaker control, thermocycler control, absorbance-reader read planning, gripper labware movement, magnetic block loading, and Flex stacker operations.
Negative fixtures preserve real analyzer error bodies for invalid deck placement and vacuum-module API-level gating.
This pack does not claim live robot HTTP /runs, /commands, gantry movement, homing, or attached-module execution response bodies.

live_boundary.boundary_statement: This source pack forbids live Opentrons robot hardware movement, run start/resume/stop actions, homing, direct motor control, and live attached-module commands.

role: Local Opentrons protocol-analysis dry-run projection for physical lab automation command plans and analyzer failures.
source_gaps: The captured response bodies are local analyzer outputs, not live robot-server HTTP /runs or /commands response bodies.
Vacuum pump commands are represented by a captured API-version gate because opentrons==9.1.0 reports MAX_SUPPORTED_VERSION 2.29 while start_set_vacuum_power requires API 2.30.
Direct robot movement, homing, run-action, and attached-module execution endpoints remain in opentrons_http_v1 until a real robot server or robot-server fixture can be captured.
